transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brought me in is... some evenings after work, I just... well, work has been a lot lately. I sell insurance, and right now everybody is calling about their policies. The phones just never stop. And my desk is right next to the breakroom, which is incredibly distracting because someone is always in there gossiping or burning popcorn. You'd think grown adults would know how to use a microwave, right? 

But anyway, I try to be really strict all day while I'm there. I'm good. But then I get home, and I end up eating way, way more than I ever meant to. Like, I'll have my normal dinner, but then suddenly I'm eating a bowl of cereal, then crackers, digging through whatever leftovers are in the fridge, finding sweets... all of it, just within a couple of hours. 

And with the price of groceries right now, it's getting expensive! I was at the store on Tuesday and a box of brand-name cereal was almost seven dollars. It's ridiculous, I don't know how families do it these days. But yeah, the eating thing in the evenings... that's why I made the appointment.
When you find yourself eating more than you meant to at home, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I get started on those nights, it's like I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm standing there telling myself to stop, I just... I can't. I don't really feel back in charge until I'm uncomfortably full. 

It reminds me of this time my sister came to visit. She lives out in Ohio now, which is a whole story on its own because she swore she'd never leave the coast, but her husband got transferred. Anyway, she came to visit and we were making this huge Thanksgiving dinner, and the oven completely broke right in the middle of roasting the turkey. Just totally died. We had to call our neighbor, Mr. Henderson—he's this lovely older man who used to be a mechanic—to see if we could use his oven. He was so sweet about it, but his kitchen was straight out of the 1970s. I mean, avocado green appliances and everything. 

But yeah, the feeling of not being able to stop... it's just awful. I just keep eating and eating.
After these episodes of eating more than you intended, do you feel distressed, guilty, or ashamed about what you've eaten?

Guilty? I'm not really sure... I haven't really noticed feeling ashamed or anything like that. I guess I just feel really physically uncomfortable, you know, from being so full. My stomach gets all stretched out and my clothes feel tight. 

Speaking of clothes, I actually had to take my favorite navy slacks to the dry cleaner on Tuesday because I spilled coffee on them at work. It was that new girl, Sarah, she bumped right into my desk while I was on a call. Anyway, I took them to the cleaner down on Elm Street—the one with the neon sign that's always flickering?—and they completely ruined the hem. Just unraveled the whole thing! I was so annoyed. I've been going to them for ten years, ever since my daughter was in high school. She used to play the flute in the marching band, and those uniforms had to be dry-cleaned constantly. They were these awful stiff wool things, and in the late summer heat during football season... oh my goodness, those poor kids were just melting out there on the field. 

But yeah, I don't know about feeling distressed or guilty. I just don't like how my pants fit after I eat that much.
After these episodes where you feel like you eat more than you intended, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising more than usual?

Well, I definitely don't make myself throw up or anything like that. But the next day after one of those nights, I'll tell myself I need to make up for it. So I'll skip breakfast and lunch, or I'll go for an extra-long hike. Sometimes I'll push myself a lot harder at my softball conditioning, even if I'm already exhausted. 

I've been playing in this adult softball league for about five years now. It's supposed to be just for fun, you know, a beer league kind of thing, but some of the women take it so seriously. Like Brenda, our pitcher. She actually bought custom cleats last season. Custom cleats! For a Wednesday night rec league! And she's always yelling at the umpire, who is usually just some high school kid trying to earn a little extra cash for the summer. It's honestly embarrassing sometimes. We play over at Centennial Park, which is beautiful, but the parking situation is just a nightmare since they started that construction on the new community center. They've had the whole north lot blocked off since April. 

But anyway, yeah, I just try to burn it off the next day by not eating until dinner or working out extra hard.
Do you find yourself having episodes where you eat a lot of food in a short amount of time, more than most people would eat under similar circumstances?

Well, yeah, I guess that's really what brought me in here in the first place. Some evenings after work, especially on days where I've been really strict and careful about what I eat all day long, I just end up eating way more than I ever meant to. It's like I'll have my regular dinner, but then I'll just keep going. I'll have a couple bowls of cereal, then half a box of crackers, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and then sweets on top of that... all within just a couple of hours. 

It usually happens when I'm watching TV. I've been trying to catch up on that new mystery series everyone at the office is talking about. You know, the one set in the Pacific Northwest with the detective who wears those chunky knit sweaters? I actually tried knitting once, back when my kids were little, but I just didn't have the patience for it. My grandmother, though, she could knit a whole afghan in a weekend. She made this gorgeous yellow one for my wedding gift, and I still have it draped over the back of my sofa. It's starting to fray a little at the edges, but I just can't bear to part with it. 

But yeah, it's just like... a whole lot of food in a really short window of time in the evenings.
During these episodes where you eat a lot in a short amount of time, do you feel like you’re not in control of yourself, like you can’t stop even if you wanted to?

Yeah, that's exactly what it feels like. Once I get started on those nights, it's like I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm standing there telling myself to stop, my hands are just reaching for another box or bag. I don't really feel back in charge of myself until I'm just uncomfortably full. 

It's kind of like when I go to Target for just one thing. You know how that is, right? You go in for laundry detergent and suddenly your cart is full of throw pillows and seasonal candles. I bought this pumpkin spice candle last week that smells exactly like the pie my Aunt Linda used to make for Thanksgiving. She always hosted Thanksgiving at her house in the Poconos. We'd drive up there every year, and the traffic on 80 was always just horrendous. My husband—well, ex-husband now—he would refuse to use the GPS, insisting he knew a shortcut through these tiny mountain towns. We always ended up lost near this one old diner with a giant plastic rooster on the roof. I wonder if that diner is still there... they had the best cherry pie. 

But anyway, yeah, it's like my brain just turns off and I can't stop eating until I physically can't fit any more in.
How often do these episodes where you feel like you can't control your eating happen? Are they happening at least once a week?

Well, yeah, I'd say for the past few months, it's been happening most weeks. Usually, it's one or two nights a week where I just eat way more than I ever planned to, and then, like I said, the next day I'm skipping meals or pushing myself extra hard on a run or at softball to make up for it. 

Speaking of softball, we actually had a game rained out last week. The weather around here has been just so unpredictable lately. One day it's sunny and seventy-five, and the next day it's pouring rain and freezing. It reminds me of this trip I took to Florida a few years ago for an insurance conference. You'd think Florida would be sunny all the time, right? But no, it rained every single afternoon right at 3 PM. You could practically set your watch by it. I was staying at this hotel that had a huge indoor atrium with all these tropical plants and a little waterfall. It was beautiful, but the humidity in there was just unbearable. My hair was frizzy the entire trip. I tried using that smoothing serum my sister recommended—she's a cosmetologist, always trying out new products—but it didn't do a thing against that Florida humidity. 

But, um, yeah, to answer your question, it's usually about once or twice a week that I have those nights where I just can't stop eating.
